title: Cahier du XVIIᵉ siècle
subtitle: Mersenne and his correspondents — Descartes, Fermat, Roberval, Pascal — with Viète before them and L'Hospital and Varignon after
rationale: The volumes of this period came into the BnF by every route the library has — the old royal collection, the Latin series, Libri's papers, later purchases — and are catalogued accordingly, by fonds and number. This cahier puts them back side by side, one mathematician to a section, in the order of their lives. The grouping is ours. Some of what is listed is autograph, some is copy made in the period; the catalogue title says which where it knows, and a volume's note says it again.

sections.title: Francesco Maurolico (1494-1575)
sections.intro: Short works on mathematics and astronomy, in one Latin volume.

sections.title: François Viète (1540-1603)
sections.intro: A volume of papers under his name.

sections.title: Claude Mydorge (1585-1647)
sections.intro: A treatise of geometry by Descartes's friend and correspondent.

sections.title: Marin Mersenne (1588-1648)
sections.intro: The friar through whom half of seventeenth-century science wrote to the other half: his papers, his work on the Bible, his remarks on the Harmonie universelle, the treatise on sound, and three volumes of the letters he received, gathered after his death by Hilarion de Coste.

sections.title: René Descartes (1596-1650)
sections.intro: His letters to Mersenne from 1638 to 1647, in two volumes, and his autograph correspondence with Constantijn Huygens.

sections.title: Pierre de Fermat (1601?-1665)
sections.intro: Mathematical memoirs under his name, and seventeenth-century copies of his letters and short works with Descartes's and Galileo's.

sections.title: Gilles Personne de Roberval (1602-1675)
sections.intro: Two volumes of papers; a treatise on mechanics of 1645 with a letter to Fermat; elements of geometry attributed to him; a miscellany with Huygens, Torricelli and Fermat.

sections.title: René-François de Sluse (1622-1685)
sections.intro: Four volumes of mathematical miscellanies by the canon of Liège.

sections.title: Blaise Pascal (1623-1662)
sections.intro: The « Recueil original » of the Pensées — his own sheets, pasted onto larger leaves — with the first copy and a later one, and a letter of 1643 to his sister. His papers bound with Mersenne's are listed under Mersenne.

sections.title: Guillaume de L'Hospital (1661-1704)
sections.intro: A manuscript of the Analyse des infiniment petits.

sections.title: Pierre Varignon (1654-1722)
sections.intro: A Latin De mecanica.

sections.title: An album of several hands
sections.intro: Autograph letters of d'Alembert, the abbé Bossut, Sophie Germain, Christiaan Huygens and Mersenne, bound together.

title: Cahier du XVIIIᵉ siècle
subtitle: Émilie du Châtelet's Newton, d'Alembert's lunar theory, Lagrange's papers and Condorcet's
rationale: Fewer volumes than either neighbour, and larger: the century's mathematicians mostly left their papers to the Académie and to Berlin and Turin, and what the BnF holds of them is what came by gift or purchase. The grouping, one section to a mathematician, is ours.

sections.title: Émilie du Châtelet (1706-1749)
sections.intro: Her French translation of Newton's Principia in three manuscript volumes, the Institutions physiques, and her letters to Maupertuis.

sections.title: Jean Le Rond d'Alembert (1717-1783)
sections.intro: Mathematical notes, and treatises on the motion of the moon and on questions of mathematics and astronomy.

sections.title: Joseph-Louis Lagrange (1736-1813)
sections.intro: One volume, « Papiers du géomètre J.-L. Lagrange », dated 1813 by the catalogue.

sections.title: Condorcet (1743-1794)
sections.intro: Letters and papers, and the notes on the progress of the human mind.

sections.title: Papers of the Académie des sciences
sections.intro: A volume of the Académie's papers holding memoirs by Clairaut and Laplace, with minutes.

title: Cahier du XIXᵉ siècle
subtitle: Fourier's twenty volumes on equations and heat, Sophie Germain's papers and letters, Libri's correspondence, Prony's journals
rationale: Three archives of very different sizes and one small piece. Fourier's papers came to the BnF as a series; Germain's and part of Libri's came when Libri's collection was seized in 1848; Prony's journals are the École des ponts' and are served by Gallica. One section to a mathematician; the grouping is ours. Germain's volumes are the ones this site has begun to transcribe.

sections.title: Joseph Fourier (1768-1830)
sections.intro: Twenty volumes of his papers: the analysis of equations, algebra, inequalities, probability and mutual insurance, geometry, mechanics, elastic plates, and seven volumes on the theory of heat. The series runs from Français 22501 to 22529; the volumes not listed here did not come up in Gallica.

sections.title: Sophie Germain (1776-1831)
sections.intro: Her papers on mathematics and physics, 750 views unsorted; her philosophical essay; the letters she received from Gauss, Legendre, Cauchy, Fourier and others; and a small volume of letters from Libri's papers. All four are transcribed on this site.

sections.title: Guillaume Libri (1803-1869)
sections.intro: Eight volumes of his correspondence and papers: letters received, notes on the manuscripts of provincial libraries, his dealings with booksellers and librarians, mathematical memoirs in three languages.

sections.title: Gaspard de Prony (1755-1839)
sections.intro: The journals of his missions in Italy, from the manuscript collection of the École des ponts et chaussées.
